description: Justified assumptions allowed in the transitive closure of the accepted bridge theorems (verification/lean/ClosureAudit.lean). Each entry is a full-match regular expression over declaration names with its justification. Anything in the closure that no entry matches rejects acceptance.

axioms.justification: Lean foundational axiom: global choice (classical logic, used by Mathlib analysis for fderiv).
Lean foundational axiom: quotient soundness (implies function extensionality).

opaque.justification: `irreducible_def` wrapper (Mathlib.Tactic.IrreducibleDef): an opaque value of the subtype {x // x = definition}; the property fixes the value, so the constant hides no freedom. Used by Mathlib (Real arithmetic, Asymptotics, FDeriv, TangentCone, Filter) and by Aeneas scalar bounds.

Lean core platform word size, only known to be 32 or 64. Aeneas usize bounds depend on it, so every theorem holds for both widths (more general than the arm64/x86_64 native targets, which are 64-bit).

Rust build configuration `cfg!(ub_checks)` (the `ub_checks` intrinsic that guards core's `assert_unsafe_precondition!` checks). It follows `debug_assertions`: native tests and debug builds run the checks, release builds do not. Aeneas translates MIR `NullaryOp(UbChecks)` to this opaque Bool, so every theorem holds for both configurations. Compiled evaluation (#eval/#guard) uses the default `false`, which is never counted as proof.

Lean core identity kept opaque for compilation. Witness path: proof terms of Lean core `grind` commutative-ring normalization (Lean.Grind.CommRing.Mon.revlexWF, well-founded recursion) used inside Mathlib lemma proofs; it occurs in proofs, not in any stated model definition.

Lean core String primitives opaque in Lean v4.29. Witness path: mkPanicMessageWithDecl <- panicWithPosWithDecl <- List.get!Internal (panic-message construction; kernel semantics of a panic return the default value, so the message string never affects a theorem).

Platform libm: values unconstrained; no accepted theorem may depend on them. `f32`/`f64` `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `atan`, `exp` and `ln` call the platform libm, whose results are not correctly rounded and differ between platforms and libm versions, so each is an opaque function with no axiom about its values (Aeneas.Std.Float); their compiled stand-in returns a NaN, so no evaluation through them is evidence. Reached by chelis-types dtype_semantics.rs:1011 apply_float_unop_f32 and :1036 apply_float_unop_f64 (FloatUnOp Exp/Log/Sin/Cos/Tan/Atan), the ActivationElement exp impls (:2112, and :2145 through f32 for f16/bf16) used by activation_sigmoid (:2167), and chelis-ir optimize.rs:117-123 (constant folding of RiscOp Exp/Log/Sin/Cos/Tan/Atan).

extern.justification: Lean core compiled implementations (@[extern]/@[implemented_by]). The kernel checks proofs against the Lean definitions; the compiled code matters only for evaluation-based evidence (#guard/#eval), which is never counted as proof.
Lean core panic reporting for compiled code; kernel semantics return the default value.

platform_assumptions.assumption: Native code runs on aarch64, where rustc lowers f32/f64 max/min to LLVM maxnum/minnum and the backend selects FMAXNM/FMINNM with FPCR.DN = 0.
platform_assumptions.justification: Rust leaves the sign of a zero result (max(-0.0, +0.0)) and NaN payloads unspecified, so no target-independent model is exact. The model is the Arm ARM FPMaxNum/FPMinNum bit for bit (-0 < +0; a quiet NaN yields the other operand; a signaling NaN yields itself quieted) and verification/float_std_models.rs and float_model_oracle.rs check it bit for bit against native code on the build host, including every signed-zero and NaN case. x86-64 lowers maxnum differently; the correspondence is claimed for aarch64 only. Reached by chelis-ir eval.rs:376 (dropout scale `1.0 / (1.0 - rate.max(0.0))`) and chelis-types fitness.rs:111 (`(unresolved_count as f64 / total as f64).min(1.0)`).

platform_assumptions.assumption: Native code runs on aarch64 with the fp16 feature (every Apple silicon host), where half 2.7.1 dispatches f16::from_f64 to FCVT Hd, Dd.
platform_assumptions.justification: FCVT is the correctly rounded IEEE conversion (round to nearest, ties to even), which the model defines as BinaryFloat.cast, with Arm FPConvertNaN payloads. The crate's software fallback (hosts without fp16/f16c) truncates the low 32 bits of the f64 first and x86 f16c converts through f32; both round twice and differ from the model on some inputs. verification/crate_model_oracle (half_model_oracle) checks the model against the crate on edge cases and dense per-exponent samples. Reached by chelis-types dtype_semantics.rs:2138 (`<half::f16 as ActivationElement>::constant`, from impl_reduced_activation_element!(half::f16) at :2164), which float_vec_activation (:2176) calls for the Sigmoid/Tanh/GELU constants on F16 buffers (:2248), among them 0.044715 and 0.7978845608028654, which are not exactly representable in f16.

platform_assumptions.item: core::hash::Hasher::write_{u16, u32, u64, u128, usize} and the signed writes through them (Aeneas.Std.Platform.littleEndian, read by Aeneas.Std.core.hash.neBytes)
platform_assumptions.assumption: Native code runs on a little-endian target (aarch64 and x86_64 are both little-endian), where an integer's `to_ne_bytes` is its `to_le_bytes`.
platform_assumptions.justification: The provided Hasher::write_* methods (core/src/hash/mod.rs) write `i.to_ne_bytes()`, whose byte order is the target's. The model states the native order once, as the named definition Aeneas.Std.Platform.littleEndian = true (Aeneas/Std/Core/Hash.lean), which core.hash.neBytes reads for every integer write; a big-endian target would have to change that definition. verification/hash_models.rs asserts `cfg!(target_endian = "little")` and checks the bytes that the derived Hash impls write against native code on the build host (aarch64), and HashModelsChecks.lean states `Platform.littleEndian = true` and that `neBytes` is `toLEBytes` under it, so renaming the assumption or changing the order fails that check. Reached by the derived Hash impls of the production crates (the isize discriminant of every derived enum Hash, and integer, str, String and Option fields); no production code hashes with a concrete Hasher (std HashMap/HashSet are banned across the workspace, crates/chelis-unord/src/lib.rs), so no production value depends on the byte order.

admission_assumptions.assumption: An Ord impl that carries #[automatically_derived] is rustc's #[derive(Ord)] expansion.
admission_assumptions.justification: The sort_unstable/sort_unstable_by models are exact only where Equal holds exactly for indistinguishable values. SortContracts admits a crate element type only if its Ord impl carries #[automatically_derived], which rustc puts on derive expansions and Charon (since 5fd1554) keeps as an unknown attribute, and every field type is admitted: the derived cmp compares the variants, then the fields in order. Rust also accepts the attribute on a hand-written impl, which is where this assumption lies; no retained production crate writes it (`automatically_derived` does not occur in crates/). Reached by chelis-types linearity.rs:311 (`ids.sort_unstable()` on Vec<BindingId>; BindingId derives Ord over u32 at linearity.rs:161).

native_models.model: Structure with the oracle schedules cancel and stack and their clocks cancelTaken and stackTaken, the guarded-frame depth (Usize), and the profiling-mark oracle profileMark with clock profileTaken. The native cancel token, stack segment size and clocks are abstracted by the oracles.
Return cancel cancelTaken and advance cancelTaken. A matching oracle is monotone (RA-g).
Return stack stackTaken and advance stackTaken. Natively exceeded(remaining_stack(), depth); every run maps to a schedule (RA-g).
depth := depth + 1, failing with integerOverflow at usize::MAX (release builds wrap, RA-h).
depth := depth.saturating_sub(1).
depth := 0.
Plain application f self through the FnOnce instance; the fresh stacker segment is not observable (RA-d).
Return profileMark profileTaken and advance profileTaken; no other field changes.
No-op: the stderr timing line is not modeled state.
FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 (ChelisModels.Sha256.digest) of the concatenated parts.
Structure with the draw oracle (Nat to Option U64) and its clock taken: the identities that the process-global counter hands to this invocation.
Return draw taken and advance taken; none is the exhaustion panic (.fail .panic). The oracle is the projection of the checked global schedule from 1 (RA-g).

Structure alpha_t of the native state of the current thread (RA-tls): flags u and o; installed, a lower bound of the process flag that the Chelis panic hook is installed (false does not mean not installed); the hook trace of (u, o, installed) per raise (the process hook suppresses a raise iff installed and (u or o)); the summary-probe count builds, nextPreflightFrame, the host inference variable oracle hostVar with clock hostVarsTaken, the environment oracle profileEnv with clock profileEnvReads, and the clock count profileMarks.
.fail .panic: the unwind leaves the enclosing native entry, outside the modeled domain; resume_unwind runs no hook (RA-b).
enter, then body, then exit on the explicit state; a failure of body propagates (the native exit on unwind is outside the modeled domain, RA-c).
Plain application f state through the FnOnce instance; red_zone and stack_size are ignored (RA-d).
Return u; the state is unchanged.
u := value.
o := value.
Append (u, o, installed) to hook and return the payload unchanged (one hook run per raise on the current thread, RA-b, RA-e).

o := true and installed := true (the hook is installed before the body), then f on (runtime, state), then o := false; the marker and message conversions of an unexpected native unwind are outside the modeled domain (RA-d, RA-f).
Return hostVar hostVarsTaken and advance hostVarsTaken. The oracle is the projection of the global fetch_add schedule from 0 (RA-g).
builds := builds.saturating_add(1).
Return builds; the state is unchanged.
builds := 0.
Return nextPreflightFrame and set it to nextPreflightFrame.wrapping_add(1).
Read profileEnv profileEnvReads and advance the clock; when enabled push a clock (profileMarks + 1, failing past usize::MAX) and return it, otherwise return 0.
No-op: the clock restart and the stderr line are not modeled state.
Return 0 for mark 0; otherwise push a clock and return the new clock count.
Return dagTotal as the new last_dag_size when start names a clock (start != 0 and start <= profileMarks), otherwise lastDagSize; the state is unchanged.
No-op: the stderr line is not modeled state.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: Every binary that links chelis-ir uses panic = unwind.
runtime_assumptions.justification: The Lean models give a native unwind the failure of the enclosing native entry, and catch_lowering, scoped exits and the child-process observations rely on catch_unwind. Under panic = abort every raise would abort the process and no catch, exit or hook suppression would run. accept.py rejects any Cargo profile or rustflags that select panic = abort; a downstream binary outside this workspace is outside the check.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: The process panic hook runs exactly once for each panic_any raise, before any destructor, on the raising thread. std::panic::resume_unwind runs no hook.
runtime_assumptions.justification: Rust std semantics of panic_any and resume_unwind (std::panic documentation). The Lean model records one hook entry per observe_raise and none for resume_native_unwind; the native child-process test records the hook and drop order of every segment.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: An unwind runs destructors innermost first; a destructor that panics during an unwind aborts the process.
runtime_assumptions.justification: Rust drop order and the double-panic abort of the std runtime. The scoped exits and the quiet-output guard of catch_native_unwind rely on the order; the hand model Unwind.lean states the abort case.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: catch_unwind returns the panic payload. stacker::grow and stacker::maybe_grow run their closure on the same thread and return its value.
runtime_assumptions.justification: std::panic::catch_unwind contract and the stacker 0.1 contract (psm switches stacks, not threads). The Lean models with_grown_stack and grow_stack_if_needed are plain application; the differential fixture and the native tests exercise the real stacker on both branches (growth and no growth).

runtime_assumptions.assumption: No code replaces the process panic hook after install_chelis_panic_hook (lowering_runtime.rs CHELIS_PANIC_HOOK_INSTALLED).
runtime_assumptions.justification: The hook suppression that the Lean model records as (u, o) per raise exists only while the Chelis hook is installed. The retained crates call set_hook only in that installer and in test code; an embedding binary that replaces the hook changes stderr only, not results.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: Destructors of typed panic payloads (LowerDiagnostic, UnrepresentableDag) have no observable effect. An abort runs no destructor, and a native stack overflow is an abort.
runtime_assumptions.justification: The payload types own plain data. The Lean models treat an abort as outside the modeled domain; the stack guards (Stack.lean) bail before an overflow, and the child-process test checks payload destruction under quiet output.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: Relaxed atomics behave as Cancellation.lean and Ids.lean state: a polling thread reads the cancellation flag in modification order with read-read coherence, and each read-modify-write reads the value of the preceding one in its modification order. stacker::remaining_stack is an arbitrary oracle, one answer per guard check.
runtime_assumptions.justification: The C++20 memory model that Rust atomics follow (coherence and RMW atomicity). No bound on visibility is assumed. The Lean oracles of cancellation_observed, stack_exhausted, fresh_host_inference_var and fresh_id are related to these native schedules by Cancellation.matched_cancel_oracle_mono, Stack.oracle_run_schedule and IdsLink.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: Release builds wrap depth += 1 in NativeServices::enter_frame (no overflow-checks), while the Lean model fails at usize::MAX; no walk nests usize::MAX guarded frames.
runtime_assumptions.justification: Each guarded frame occupies native stack, and a thread stack holds far fewer than usize::MAX frames before the guards bail; so the wrap and the model failure are both unreachable. Stack.cn_enter_frame_overflow states the model side.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: No native primitive runs inside a thread-local destructor (for example during the destruction of PROFILE_MARKS or NATIVE_LOWERING_STATE).
runtime_assumptions.justification: Accessing a thread local during its destruction panics or reinitializes it, which the Lean models do not describe. No Drop impl of the retained crates calls a lowering primitive; the primitives run only inside extracted calls that the native adapters make.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: No DiagnosticSink is visible after an unwind: chelis-types has no non-test catch_unwind, so an unwinding checker entry drops its sink with its skipped scope exits.
runtime_assumptions.justification: session.rs sink scopes run their exit only on return. A sink is opened by a session.rs checker entry and owned by it, and no other crate can construct or hold a sink; so a catch outside the checker only sees the entry return by unwinding. accept.py rejects any catch_unwind in non-test chelis-types code.

runtime_assumptions.assumption: alpha_t: the native state of thread t (NATIVE_LOWERING_STATE, PROFILE_MARKS, this thread's draws from NEXT_HOST_INFERENCE_VAR, the environment reads) maps to one Lean LoweringRuntime value. Every primitive call sequence on t, through any number of nested with_native_lowering_runtime handles, moves alpha_t as the Lean models specify, in program order.
runtime_assumptions.justification: LoweringRuntime is a field-less handle that is neither Send nor Sync (compile_fail doc-tests), so every primitive call through it runs on the thread that acquired it, and nested handles name the same thread-local state. The hook reads only the flags of the raising thread. The internal shell items (state, entries, helpers) have zero core dependents in both strict plans (accept.py), so extracted code reaches the state only through the primitives. The coverage check on a whole-core extraction is the remaining structural check.
